Group: R10-FLOW-ANDON (registration pending: roster PR-B). Spec: pack file `dev/programme/flow-study/roster/groups/R10-FLOW-ANDON.json` at pin ff1beba2a24cab268cca5426cc390dbf21185cc0 (Lean study K8). Countermeasure for R10-RCA-ORCH-CONTINUITY (cited, not redone): two orchestrator stops went unnoticed for 6 h and 16 h because no loop wrote a liveness signal readable off the host.

Each `tick_loop.sh` pass now calls `heartbeat.sh --once`, which force-pushes `heartbeat/orchestrator` (parentless empty-tree commit, message `TICK-PASS <utc> relay=<..> tick=<rc>`, no host path) with the seat's credential, `-f --no-verify`, message through `ref_privacy.py guard`. A failed push prints `HEARTBEAT NOT PUSHED: <reason>` and the loop goes on. `heartbeat.sh --watch [--max-age 1200]` is the owner-side watcher's command (exit 1 and `HEARTBEAT STALE` past 20 min or when the ref is absent). Per the Seam carry it is a standalone job script with `--once`, not entrenched in `tick_loop.sh`. Alternative rejected: writing the push inline in `tick_loop.sh` (the design retires that file).

Round 2: `heartbeat.sh` is registered `guarded` in `ref_privacy.py`'s `PUSHERS` (it already called `ref_privacy.py guard --ref`; the registry did not name it, so `instrument-self-tests`' ref_privacy step refused its push site). The guard arm of `heartbeat.sh --self-test` now runs against the reachable bare remote and asserts the ref did not move, so it fails if the guard is skipped rather than only if a push errors; mutant `heartbeat-4` deletes the guard call. Alternative rejected: registering the file as `fixture` or another unguarded disposition, which would be false, since the production `--once` path pushes a caller-supplied message.

## Head

`9e7f601031512fd510029675b4a84df8bb2204d1` merges main `1602f93` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`be4158a763f122732bc687b9b0170e7908433a19` merges main `07fcbee` into the previous head: an automatic merge by the orchestrator, no resolution. The reviewed code is unchanged.

`c8b85d11564a9f429fafbe3353a4b8746e45b187` merges the authored code head `841c65da4deed8c78dd73616b56aa0661b830c3a` and then merges origin/main `46e368127` (an automatic merge by the orchestrator's script; any resolution inside the code head is described below) into this PR's previous head.

Code head: the tip of `handoff/r10-flow-andon` (841c65da4deed8c78dd73616b56aa0661b830c3a), the merge of origin/main 5a755f53efda (#2529) into PR head 7a3fc062b4cfe43acc34dc24481dd21bc1a073ac (merge, not rebase). Figures below were taken at that head against origin/main 5a755f53efda, 2026-10-21T22:34Z. `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` is clean at that tip; at 7a3fc062b it exits 1 (the conflict this round resolves).

## Conflict resolution

One file, `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`, two hunks, both resolved by keeping both sides:
- The module docstring's id sentence: main says `S01..S38 each plant one production-line`, this branch said `S01..S34 and the per-file ids (tick_loop-N, heartbeat-N) each plant...`. Kept: `S01..S38 and the per-file ids (tick_loop-N, heartbeat-N) each plant one production-line`.
- The tail of `MUTANTS`: main appended S35..S38 (#2444's forward-carry: three `handoff_push.sh` push lines and the `merge_pr.sh` merge line), this branch appended tick_loop-1, tick_loop-2, heartbeat-1..heartbeat-4. Kept main's four first, then this branch's six, each tuple byte-identical to its side.
No other file conflicted; the rest of #2529 (governance.yml, closure.py, closures.json, INSTRUMENTS.md, cloud_relay.sh, handoff_push.sh, a new harness and two delivery rows) merged automatically.

## Mutation proof

`python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py` (every mutant, at 841c65da4) -> `M0: 0 seat step(s) red`, then every mutant `KILLED`, `RESULT survivors=0`, exit 0.
- This PR's six: tick_loop-1 KILLED (heartbeat call deleted), tick_loop-2 KILLED (`tick_loop self-test: 12 checks, 1 failed`), heartbeat-1..heartbeat-4 KILLED (each `heartbeat self-test: 7 checks, 1 failed`).
- Main's four from #2529: S35, S36, S37 KILLED (each `handoff_push self-test: 2 checks, 1 failed`), S38 KILLED (`merge_pr self-test: 16 checks, 2 failed`).
- S01..S34, S04U and W1..W3 also KILLED.

## Null control

For the resolution keeping both sides: a scratch probe parses the `MUTANTS` id set at three revisions (`ast` over `git show <rev>:<path>`). It prints `main=35 branch=37 head=41 union=41 missing_from_head=[] extra_in_head=[]` and exits 0 at HEAD. Run with origin/main in HEAD's place (a main-side-only resolution) it lists the six andon ids missing and exits 1. Run with 7a3fc062b in HEAD's place (a branch-side-only resolution) it lists S35..S38 missing and exits 1. For the mutants, M0 in the same harness run runs every `instrument-self-tests` seat step unmutated and every step is rc=0, so each KILLED is the mutant's. Round 2's registry null control (`ref_privacy.py --check` refuses heartbeat.sh at 5005f02ef) is not affected by this merge and was not re-taken.

## Figures

All at 841c65da4, origin/main 5a755f53efda, 2026-10-21T22:34Z:
- `python3 dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py` -> `RESULT survivors=0`, M0 `0 seat step(s) red`
- `bash tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh --self-test` -> `heartbeat self-test: 7 checks, 0 failed`
- `bash tools/audit/seat/tick_loop.sh --self-test` -> `tick_loop self-test: 12 checks, 0 failed`
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --check` -> ref_privacy's own summary line, `0 refused`
- `python3 -I tools/audit/seat/ref_privacy.py --self-test` -> `0 failed`
- `python3 tools/audit/seat/selftest_wiring.py --check` -> its own summary line, 0 unwired
- `python3 tests/throwaway_git.py --check` -> 0 refused
- `python3 tests/structure.py` -> STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED; no budget raised
- `python3 tests/closure.py select --diff $(git merge-base origin/main HEAD)` -> MODE: SCOPED, runs tests/entities.py and tests/harness_headers.py
- `tests/entities.py` (seat venv, PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub) -> ALL ENTITY CHECKS PASSED
- `tests/harness_headers.py` (seat venv, PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub) -> ALL HARNESS HEADER CHECKS PASSED

## Red checks

At PR head 7a3fc062b the one red check is `nightly-status`. This head has not run CI yet; it inherits that check's input unchanged. `nightly-status` grades the scheduled runs on `main`, not this diff. Its failing inputs are main's nightly lanes. This diff touches no production module, no `tests/` driver, no budget and no `tests.yml`. Its `governance.yml` hunk adds one step to `instrument-self-tests`, which no nightly job runs. The cheaper detector for main's nightly reds is the PR-time `mutation` job and the scoped gate, which already run on every pull request and were green at 7a3fc062b. Carry: dismissed: main's nightly lanes, not this diff

`ci-ratchet` was skipped on this PR. Main's own red there is runner-speed variance, and R10-CI-LAYOUT owns it. It is not this diff's: this diff adds no CI job and changes no budget. Carry: R10-CI-LAYOUT

`instrument-self-tests`: read from the check-runs API per commit (`repos/tvofi/heatpump_optimizer/commits/<sha>/check-runs`, 2026-10-22). It concluded `failure` at 8f5807ae45b079dc5978e925b3f56fb2008af3fc (round 1 head, completed 2026-10-21T17:56:21Z) on an unregistered push site (`heartbeat.sh` absent from `ref_privacy.py`'s `PUSHERS`), and round 2 fixed that cause. It concluded `success` at 7a3fc062b4cfe43acc34dc24481dd21bc1a073ac (completed 2026-10-21T21:10:47Z), and 841c65da4 has no check run yet. The harness M0 above re-runs every step of that job green at 841c65da4. Carry: dismissed: fixed in round 2, green at 7a3fc062b

## Forward-carry

- The owner-side watcher (a scheduled cloud task every 15 min running `tools/audit/seat/heartbeat.sh --watch`, notify on exit 1) is not scheduled in the tree and needs the owner to schedule it. Carry: dismissed: owner-scheduled by design (K8 "no repo change"), stated in INSTRUMENTS.md.
- R10-ORCH-MACHINERY must register `heartbeat.sh --once` as the beat's heartbeat job and then drop the call from `tick_loop.sh`. Carry: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY

## Friction

- Finder's harness (step 2). The finder's harness is the CI ref_privacy step. I ran `ref_privacy.py --check` at 5005f02ef and at the head, and I ran the committed mutant harness myself. Both ends match the body.

The commit message carried from tick_loop is `TICK-PASS <utc> relay=<rc> tick=<rc>`, with no --out path. - Class (step 6). The group has one seam (one liveness ref) and the body names no enumeration rule. The class is that one seam.
- Red checks (step 11). pr-contract's range read is `record red-history 6 commits: instrument-self-tests, nightly-status`. instrument-self-tests is green at this head and the body answers it with a cheaper detector: `ref_privacy.py --check`, which costs seconds. nightly-status is answered truthfully. The body names its own governance.yml touch, which is why it owes the answer. nightly-status grades main's scheduled run 39563978649 (c77f89d, 07:43Z), and I confirmed from that run's logs: slow fails at `loop_cpu_ratio 0.1138 over its budget 0.111`, and mutation-nightly at `10 survivor(s) of 23 evaluated = 39.1% ... cap 30.0%`, all in custom_components/. #2548 merged at 17:03Z. The pr-contract run 119413000833 started 18:42:00, after nightly-status concluded red at 18:41:43, and passed: PR-BODY 0 errors, FIGURES 11 resolved, CARRY-AUDIT 2 routed, 0 unrouted.
- Head SHA (step 7). The body names 83d9662d8c75 and its code head a50dee030. Both match what I measured.
- Forward-carry (step 10). R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's job is to register `heartbeat.sh --once` as the beat's heartbeat job. That instruction is already written: the spec pin's shadow roster carries it in R10-ORCH-MACHINERY's own carry (K17: "heartbeat (R10-FLOW-ANDON's job script; interval 300 s, timeout 60 s ...)"), and so do FUTURE-STATE.md's folded carries. It is not yet on origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster (23ef06dc), because the pack's groups are "registration pending: roster PR-B", as the title says. The roster registration carries it there, so I do not block.

## Round

Re-review at a moved head (round 3 of the review; the earlier verdict at 83d9662d was merge). Head reviewed: `c8b85d11564a9f429fafbe3353a4b8746e45b187`, re-read as the PR head before writing. The head moved only by merges: c1b8252dc (7a3fc062b + 841c65da4) and c8b85d11564a9f429fafbe3353a4b8746e45b187 (c1b8252dc + origin/main 46e368127); both trees equal `git merge-tree --write-tree` of their parents, so both are automatic. The one hand resolution is inside 841c65da4 (the `r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py` docstring and MUTANTS tail), judged below. Apart from that hunk, the PR's own diff against origin/main is byte-identical to its diff at 83d9662d (only hunk offsets differ).

## Findings

- Surviving mutant: replacing `--max-age) max=${2:-}; shift 2 || shift ;;` with `--max-age) shift 2 || shift ;;` (the option is parsed but ignored, so the age limit is always 1200) leaves `heartbeat.sh --self-test` at 7 checks, 0 failed. Its two watcher fixtures (fresh at --max-age 600, 1800 s stale at --max-age 1200) give the same result under the default. My hand null control shows the arm works at this head (900 s old: STALE under --max-age 600, FRESH under 1200), and the owner's watcher uses the default. So this is a test gap, not a defect: the self-test should add one fixture whose verdict flips with --max-age (for example 900 s old under 600). Evidence: ev/own_mutants.txt R4, ev/null_controls_watch.txt. Carry: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY
- The roster carry "Revision 12" on R10-FLOW-ANDON (origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster 743463c61, added in 735981f4e at 2026-10-21T20:42Z) asks for three more alarms: a handoff tip ahead of its PR head for over 20 minutes, a lock whose owner pid is dead, and a seat self-test process older than 1 h. This PR does none of them and its body does not mention them. The heartbeat this PR lands is the group's K8 brief and is complete on its own, so the gap does not block this merge, but the alarms are still owed after it. Carry: R10-FLOW-ANDON
- Self-test hygiene item (a) in the same roster carry says a new mutant "sits inside the block of the instrument it tests, never appended at the file's end". tick_loop-1 and tick_loop-2 come after S35..S38 at the end of MUTANTS, not next to tick_loop's S31..S34. The ids follow the per-file convention and the merge with #2529 resolved cleanly. Whoever next adds mutants to that file should move them. Carry: R10-ORCH-MACHINERY

## Evidence

- Mutation proof (finder's seat harness `dev/audit/harnesses/r10_seat_selftests_mutants.py`, run in full at the head): `M0: 0 seat step(s) red`, 48 KILLED, `RESULT survivors=0`, exit 0. The six from this PR are tick_loop-1, tick_loop-2 and heartbeat-1..4, all KILLED. #2529's S35..S38 are KILLED too (ev/mutants_head.txt).
- My own mutants at the head (ev/own_mutants.txt): R1, a host path (`out=$out`) in the heartbeat message, is KILLED (2 tick_loop checks fail). R2, a failed heartbeat aborting the pass, is KILLED (1 fails). R3, the watcher comparison inverted, is KILLED (2 fail). R5, the commit gaining a parent, is KILLED (3 fail). R4 survives (see Findings).
- Both ends (ev/both_ends.txt): main's tick_loop.sh --once against a bare remote leaves no heartbeat/orchestrator ref, and the head's watcher prints `HEARTBEAT STALE: no heartbeat/orchestrator` with rc=1. The head's tick_loop.sh --once moves the ref to `TICK-PASS <utc> relay=absent tick=0`, with no host path and no parent, and the watcher prints `HEARTBEAT FRESH` with rc=0.
- Null controls for the --watch --max-age arm (ev/null_controls_watch.txt): under the default 1200 s limit, ages 60 and 1190 are FRESH (rc 0) and 1260 and 3600 are STALE (rc 1, naming the message). A 900 s ref is STALE under --max-age 600 and FRESH under 1200. A non-numeric --max-age exits 2. A message carrying $HOME is refused (`HEARTBEAT NOT PUSHED: ref_privacy guard refused the message`, rc 1).
- The loop continues on a failed push. tick_loop's self-test checks "a failing heartbeat is printed ... loop still exits cleanly" and "null control: a refused push is printed with its reason and the pass still completes", and both are ok. heartbeat.sh pushes with `-f --no-verify` (heartbeat-1 KILLED).
- Resolution null control (my probe, ev/ids_probe.py, ev/ids_null_control.txt): at the head it prints `main=35 branch=37 head=41 union=41 missing_from_head=[]`, rc 0. With origin/main in the head's place, the six andon ids are missing (rc 1). With 7a3fc062b in its place, S35..S38 are missing (rc 1). This re-derives the body's figures.
- Every figure in the body was re-taken at this head, not at 841c65da4 as the body took them (ev/figures_head.txt):
  - heartbeat self-test: 7 checks, 0 failed. Re-derived.
  - tick_loop self-test: 12 checks, 0 failed. Re-derived.
  - ref_privacy --check: 0 refused (20 files with a push site, 10 guarded). Re-derived.
  - ref_privacy --self-test: 66 checks, 0 failed. Re-derived.
  - selftest_wiring: 73 self-testing, 73 wired, 0 unwired. Re-derived.
  - throwaway_git: 0 refused. Re-derived.
  - STRUCTURE RATCHET PASSED, no budget file in the diff. Re-derived.
  - closure select: `MODE: SCOPED -- 2 script(s) run`, the scripts being entities.py and harness_headers.py. Re-derived.
  - harness_headers: ALL 109 PASSED. Re-derived.
  - entities.py (venv-ci, PYTHONPATH=tests/hastub): the first run printed `1 of 2382 ENTITY CHECKS FAILED`. It ran alongside the mutation harness and my mutant worktree, and I captured only its tail. The re-run alone printed `ALL 2382 ENTITY CHECKS PASSED` (ev/entities_rerun_head.txt). I count the figure as re-derived on the re-run. I could not identify the first run's failing check.
  - Not re-derivable here: the body's timestamp and its claim that the figures were "at 841c65da4 against 5a755f53efda", which describe the fixer's run. The same numbers hold at this head.
- Merge-tree: `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main c8b85d11564a9f429fafbe3353a4b8746e45b187` exits 0, and its tree e3b2f51d0 equals the head's tree (ev/merge_tree.txt). The merge base is origin/main 46e368127, so the head is 0 commits behind.
- roles/: `git diff merge-base...origin/main -- dev/governance/roles/` is empty, so the contract read is current.
- VERSION, the manifest, RELEASE_NOTES and both claim files are untouched (ev/head_chain.txt).
- carry_audit over the PR body (`--roster-ref origin/handoff/audit-r10-roster check`): `3 finding item(s): 3 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)` (ev/carry_audit_body.txt).
- CI on this head, from the check-runs API per commit (ev/check_runs.txt, ev/check_runs_final.txt):
  - instrument-self-tests, mutation, closures, closure-scope, scope, coverage, coverage-ratchet, arch-score, budget-raise-gate, briefs, policy-docs, typing, lane-proofs, fast (3.14), browser, env-matrix, hassfest, validate-hacs, delivery-status, wave-script, graders-head-copy and CodeQL Analyze all succeeded. pr-contract succeeded twice, and a third run was in progress at the final read.
  - c1b8252dc and 841c65da4 carry no check runs.
- Red checks: `nightly-status` failed. It grades main's scheduled lanes, and this diff reaches nothing it reads (no production module, tests/ driver, budget or tests.yml). The body names and answers it. ci-ratchet did not run on this head, and main's red there is runner-speed variance owned by R10-CI-LAYOUT, which the body also answers.
- Mutation lane: green. The diff writes no production code line (only seat tools, a workflow step, a harness, docs and a delivery row), so the lane draws no mutant and its green does not show that mutants were evaluated.
- Forward-carry: the body routes R10-ORCH-MACHINERY to register `heartbeat.sh --once` as the beat's job, and dismisses the owner-scheduled watcher by design.
- carry_audit over this verdict: read whole, it prints `0 finding item(s)`, because `## Findings` is not a heading the tool reads as notes. Read with this verdict's `## Findings` bullets placed under `## Forward-carry`, it prints `3 finding item(s): 3 routed, 0 unrouted, 0 bad destination(s)`.
